The Federal Character Commission has uncovered 317 alleged cases of compromise and replacement of candidates in the Nigeria Customs Service recruitment exercise following a review of the process. The commission, however, has lifted the temporary suspension placed on the training of 3,852 newly recruited personnel after a week of meetings and consultations with the management of the service. In a statement released on Saturday in Abuja, the FCC spokesperson, Ademola Lawrence, said the commission reviewed recruitment records, examined complaints from affected candidates and investigated allegations surrounding the exercise during the suspension. The commission said 576,000 applicants initially applied for the recruitment, while 3,852 candidates made the initial final list. It added that 505 candidates were subsequently disqualified or affected by changes to the list for various reasons. Giving details of its findings, the FCC said, “A total of 317 candidates were identified in connection with cases of alleged compromise and replacement of other candidates in the recruitment process. It also disclosed that 126 candidates were disqualified for reasons including failed drug tests, certificate falsification and age discrepancies, while 62 candidates on the initial final list failed to report for the exercise. According to the FCC, 2,696 personnel are currently undergoing training, while arrangements are being made for the second batch. Explaining its intervention, the commission said it was aimed at ensuring fairness in the recruitment process and guaranteeing that qualified Nigerians from all parts of the country were given equal opportunities. Customs launches 79-episode television series, Novara Customs CG wants competent officers to sustain reforms DSS, Customs strengthen airport security partnership in Lagos “The Commission’s intervention was to ensure that the recruitment process was fair and that qualified Nigerians from all parts of the country were given equal consideration,” the statement added. The FCC said it would continue to monitor the remaining stages of the recruitment exercise to ensure compliance with approved Federal Character guidelines. It also urged candidates who had genuine reasons to challenge their exclusion from the exercise to submit complaints through its dedicated WhatsApp numbers. The commission stressed that its responsibility was not to obstruct the activities of government institutions but to ensure that qualified Nigerians had fair opportunities in federal employment, irrespective of their states of origin or geopolitical zones. The intervention, it said, was carried out in line with Section 14(3) and Paragraph 8, Part I of the Third Schedule to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, and the Federal Character Commission Act. “The Commission remains resolute in its commitment to constitutionalism, meritocracy, equitable representation, national integration and good governance. “Equity remains a constitutional obligation and not an administrative privilege,” it said. On November 21, the Nigeria Customs Service announced the suspension of training activities for 3,852 newly recruited officers, nearly two years after the recruitment process began.
